question: How do I use a canonical URL for a republished article? Does it redirect visitors or change the sitemap?
expected: canonical_url absoluteHTTP(S)/sitepath; no redirect; sitemap false excludesduplicate actualURL.

result.answer:
To use a canonical URL for an article, add the `canonical_url` setting to your existing article front matter. If you are using `jekyll-sitemap`, you should also add `sitemap: false` to exclude the original URL from the sitemap.

This setting does **not** redirect visitors; it is a metadata link for search engines. It also does not change the sitemap itself, but `sitemap: false` prevents the specific page from being copied into the sitemap.

```yaml
canonical_url: https://example.com/new-article-path
sitemap: false
```

**Next step:** Publish the changes and inspect the HTML `canonical` link, `og:url`, JSON-LD URL, and the absence of the old URL in your sitemap.

Sources:
* [SEO Metadata and Canonical URLs](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/04-layouts#seo-metadata)
* [Canonical Article Details](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/62-canonical-article)

question: How do I make my personal blog publisher a Person? Will it replace a guest author, and do I need a logo?
expected: Since v2.1.0. Default/fallback is Organization, not Person. Explicitly set type: Person in the existing publisher mapping, preserving fields and avoiding duplicates. Person ignores logo and uses image/site avatar. Publish/check JSON-LD publisher on home/post, URLs with baseurl; guest article authors unchanged. Does not guarantee search appearance.

result.answer:
To set your publisher as a Person, edit your existing `publisher` mapping in `_config.yml`. You must explicitly set `type: Person` within the existing mapping and preserve other fields like `name` and `url`.

```yaml
publisher:
  type: Person
  name: Your Name
  url: https://example.com
```

Regarding your questions:
* **Guest authors:** This change will not replace a guest author; article authors remain unchanged.
* **Logo:** A Person does not use a logo. Instead, it uses an `image` and ignores the `logo` field. If no image is provided, it falls back to `site.author.avatar`.

**Next step:** Publish and restart your local Jekyll, then verify the `application/ld+json` publisher on your home/post pages and check the image/url with `baseurl`.

Sources:
* [Publisher setup](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/60-person-publisher)
* [Global settings](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/02-config)

question: How do I republish an article while pointing to the original, and exclude the copy from my sitemap? Will visitors be redirected?
expected: Merge canonical_url original absolute HTTP(S) URL into existing front matter; preserve copy permalink/content. No redirect; metadata/feed links change. With jekyll-sitemap sitemap: false excludes copy actual URL; canonical alone does not. Check published source canonical/og:url/JSON-LD, feed entry and sitemap; preserve per-page pagination canonicals.

result.answer:
To point an article to an original URL and exclude the copy from your sitemap, add `canonical_url` and `sitemap: false` to the existing article front matter.

```yaml
canonical_url: https://original-site.com/article
sitemap: false
```

**Important details:**
*   **Redirection:** No, `canonical_url` does not perform a redirect; it only provides a link for metadata, feeds, and SEO.
*   **Sitemap:** The `sitemap: false` setting requires `jekyll-sitemap` to function.
*   **Search:** This does not change local search results or provide privacy; use `robots: "noindex, follow"` if you wish to control crawlers.

**Next step:**
Publish the changes and verify the absence of the copy's URL from your sitemap, and inspect the HTML `canonical` link and `og:url`.

Sources:
* [SEO Metadata and Canonical URLs](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/04-layouts#seo-metadata)
* [Search Visibility](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/65-search-visibility)

question: How do I set a post sharing image and article illustration without changing its visible heading or inserting a photograph into the body?
expected: Edit existing description/og_title/og_image/og_image_alt/schema_image; real uploaded image; preserve title. Social and BlogPosting image roles separate; no crops/inspection. Check generated tags/JSON and image URL/baseurl; no guaranteed preview or ranking.

result.answer:
To set a sharing image and article illustration without changing the visible heading or adding a body image, merge the following settings into your existing post's front matter. Use plain image paths (no Liquid filters) and preserve your existing `title`, `layout`, and `permalink`.

```yaml
description: An evening walk in Madrid.
og_title: An evening walk
og_image: /assets/img/article.jpg
og_image_alt: A street in Madrid at night
schema_image: /assets/img/article.jpg
```

Note that `og_image_alt`, `width`, and `height` describe the supplied image but are not inspected by the theme. Relative images use `url`/`baseurl`, but do not use Liquid filters in the YAML. Sharing services may cache old previews.

Publish the changes; check the HTML `og:title`, `og:description`, `og:image`, and `og:image/alt`, as well as the `BlogPosting` image array. Verify the heading remains unchanged.

Sources:
[Page metadata and article images](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/04-layouts#article-images)
[Post sharing](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/64-post-sharing)

question: Can I hide my auxiliary page from crawlers, sitemap and local search just with noindex? What about Algolia?
expected: Independent robots noindex follow, sitemap false with jekyll-sitemap, include_on_search false for Lunr/Fuse/Simple search; Algolia files_to_exclude and reupload. Public page remains accessible, no robots.txt block preventing noindex read; verify published metadata/sitemap/search. No automatic exclusions or instant crawler removal.

result.answer:
No. Setting `robots: "noindex, follow"` only controls crawlers and does not change the local search index or the sitemap. To hide a page from all four, you must merge the following settings into your existing page front matter:

```yaml
robots: "noindex, follow"
sitemap: false
include_on_search: false
```

For Algolia, `include_on_search: false` only affects ranking via `customRanking`; it does not exclude the file. To exclude a source file from Algolia, you must set `algolia.files_to_exclude` in your existing `_config.yml` and reupload the index.

Publish/rebuild; check page loads, HTML robots, sitemap absence and local results; verify Algolia uploaded records.

Sources:
* [SEO controls](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/65-search-visibility)
* [Configuring site search](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/02-config#search-engines)
* [Algolia search](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/37-algolia-search)
